A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SwiftKV and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Their corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and the appendices report original model-quality, throughput, latency, ablation, and early-exit results.

after.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendices A–B retain original empirical results and add comparator evaluations, Qwen results, and SGLang/ShareGPT serving measurements.

M1.justification: SingleInputKV is renamed SwiftKV, but the shared-input KV projections, AcrossKV sharing, and partial-QKV distillation remain unchanged. The optional early-exit head, combined distillation loss, and 0.95 exit threshold also survive in Appendix B.4. SGLang integration does not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Appendix A.5 substantially extends serving evaluation from synthetic requests to actual ShareGPT conversations, including heterogeneous request distributions filtered by input/output ratios. The reported distillation mixture also adds SlimOrca to Ultrachat and OpenHermes-2.5. The seven model-quality evaluation settings and earlier math/code and Alpaca analyses remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds FFN-SkipLLM comparisons for Llama-8B, Llama-3B, Mistral, Deepseek, and Qwen; Nemotron-51B for the Llama-70B comparison; and DarwinLM-8.4B for Qwen. These introduce direct pruning/skipping competitors beyond v2's original-model baselines and retained compression/distillation controls.

E3.justification: New protocols cover Qwen2.5-14B configurations, SGLang serving, ShareGPT ratio filtering, and the added competitors. The stated Llama-405B precision changes from W8A8 to W8A16. Appendix training-data size changes from 160M to 680M tokens, although v2's main text already stated 680M; these reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The ShareGPT ratio study tests whether throughput benefits persist under heterogeneous requests and different prompt/output balances, while SGLang provides an additional check across serving systems. Existing distillation, memory, quantization, inter/intra-layer sharing, dataset, and early-exit analyses are retained, often relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for performance. The early-exit probability distribution and alignment analysis are retained without a changed uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Corresponding earlier quality and ablation table values are retained, while v3 adds substantial comparator, Qwen, SGLang, and ShareGPT results. For example, Table 2 newly reports Qwen averages of 77.38 for the original model, 76.23 at 25% SwiftKV, and 69.93 at 50%. These are additional results under specified configurations, not improvements over corresponding v2 measurements.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 retain the same similarity definition, KV projection construction, and teacher/student formulation. The compute-reduction reasoning and appendix early-exit formulation also remain equivalent. No new theorem, proof, or substantive formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction recast AcrossKV as optional support for low-memory scenarios and emphasize model-dependent 25–50% prefill reduction. They add an explicit distillation-efficiency comparison with pruning methods. The central model-transformation contribution and headline throughput/latency claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds GPU-time contention as an explanation for improved decode latency and suggests lower layer similarity explains Qwen's larger degradation. It removes explicit discussion of unexplored DPO/RLHF and pretraining, plus v2's explanation of decoding and serving overheads limiting speedup. Dataset-quality and early-exit qualifications remain in the appendices.

D1.justification: V3 adds direct training/inference repository pointers and documents SGLang support, but removes several reproduction details: training batch size 32, the 50-example similarity-estimation sample, explicit MMLU chat-template flags, GEMM fusion and cache-allocation optimizations, and the FP8 dtype. These omissions span training, evaluation, and serving; they do not establish removal of the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned toward pruning and layer skipping, adding discussion of FFN-SkipLLM, Nemotron/Minitron, DarwinLM, LayerSkip, SliceGPT, and other pruning approaches. The former hardware/system-optimization survey is removed, and new dataset and SGLang references support the expanded empirical positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and results narrative are extensively rewritten, with SingleInputKV renamed throughout. Experimental sections are reorganized, Appendices A–F become A–B, quantization discussion moves to the appendix, and duplicated early-exit explanation is consolidated.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to two columns. Separate main-text and appendix quality tables are consolidated into Table 2; Tables A.2–A.3 are added; the large-model similarity panel moves into Figure 2; and other displays are relocated or resized. Figure 4 also changes latency-axis units from milliseconds to seconds without establishing changed results.

improvement.justification: The new direct competitors in Table 2 and SGLang/ShareGPT tests in Tables A.2–A.3 improve comparative and practical validation, while Qwen results expose a useful applicability boundary. These gains are partly offset by removed reproducibility details and limitations, an ambiguous FFN-SkipLLM depth range in Table 2's caption, and an unreconciled relationship between the revised training recipe and retained dataset analysis. The net improvement is therefore limited.
